**Step:** [step-3](../README.md) — Does an unbiased genome-wide ranking driven by the child's HPO terms agree with the panel-first candidate list?
**Status:** supported  |  **Confidence:** 0.80  |  **Revisions:** 2
**Gene:** BUB1B  |  **Path:** path 1 × phenotype

## The claim

Among all genes that carry a candidate biallelic set of rare protein-altering PASS alleles genome-wide, BUB1B is the best-ranked gene in the panel-blind phenotype ranking — the two independent signals (DNA-derived biallelic set, symptom-derived gene rank) converge on one gene.

**Prediction if true.** Ordering results.gene_biallelic rows with biallelic_pass true by phenotype_rank ascending puts BUB1B first; the second-ranked biallelic gene has a phenotype rank worse than BUB1B's.

**What would refute it.** A different biallelic_pass gene with a better (smaller) phenotype rank than BUB1B.

## Evidence

| # | Direction | Strength | Kind | Observation | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 15 | supports | 0.70 | measurement | Ordering the 65 biallelic-on-PASS genes by the panel-blind phenotype rank puts BUB1B first at rank 6; the next curated biallelic gene is HSPG2 at rank 150, then PEX5 at 220. Forty-one of the 65 have no HPO curation at all. | `methodology/071` |
| 16 | neutral | 0.00 | absence | The two instruments share no data (the ranking reads ontology files, the scan reads the callset) but the panel that motivated the scan was chosen from the same literature the HPO annotations summarise, so convergence is strong corroboration, not fully independent confirmation. | `methodology/071` |
